status: design: geometry is the design's; heights, cover, separations and gate ground are measured against the rasters by net_checks.py; triangles, bytes, texture, draw calls and collision are estimates
name: The Undermere
frame: the village's: x east, y north, z up, metres; every passage point is a floor point

look.note: one look for every cave, the same JSON values exactly

difficulty.crawl: D1: clear at least 1.25 m and at most 8 m long; D2: clear 1.10-1.25 m or 8-15 m long; D3: clear under 1.10 m, or over 15 m, or a wet or loose floor with a bend; a wet or loose floor is at least D2
difficulty.sidle: D1: at least 0.53 m wide and at most 7 m long; D2: 0.47-0.53 m or 7-12 m; D3: under 0.47 m or over 12 m; a kink is at least D2 (D3 under 0.47 m)
difficulty.climb: D1: at most 3 m with good holds; D2: 3-6 m, or wet and at most 3 m; D3: over 6 m, or wet and over 3 m
difficulty.depth_bands: a move on a gate-to-gate route has the difficulty of its depth: D1 at or above z -10, D2 from -10 to -25, D3 below -25; a side trip may be harder than its band

rules.cover: ground.npz height minus the roof (floor + clear height + 0.5 m natural, 0.3 m mine) at least 2 m, except in a gate's mouth zone (mouth_zone_m; at the Adit Gate, behind the grille at the end of its cutting, at least 0.6 m of today's ground over the roof in the first metre and 1.0 m beyond, walls included) and at declared openings (shafts and the Chink, each over its own column); climb faces are sampled foot to top plus clear height
rules.separation: two places close in space but far apart on foot have at least 0.6 m of rock between their envelopes (clear core + 0.3 m natural / 0.15 m mine wall allowance)
rules.walk: ramps at most 20 degrees, stairs at most 37 degrees with risers 0.25 m, clear at least 0.8 x 2.1 m; every drop over 0.35 m is a climb face (its own way back) or a declared one-way drop with a way back
rules.fissure_build: a sidle passage (profile fissure, zone wall_noise 0) is built with smooth walls: no noise on its two walls within 0.3 m of body height (0.35 to 1.75 m above the floor), and after meshing every 0.25 m along it the clear gap at 0.5, 1.0 and 1.5 m above the floor is measured on the mesh and must be at least 0.40 m (the sidling body is 0.36 m across; the design widths are 0.43 to 0.55 m, at 0.125 m cells)

gates.name: the Adit Gate
gates.village_name: Mill Lane and the Lumber Mill
gates.device: a Company grille with one lamp
gates.sees: Vane's adit: off the outlaws' trail a stone-lined cutting runs due east into the rising ground, 2.0 m wide between dry-stone walls that grow from nothing at the trail to 3.5 m at the portal and carry a dry-stone parapet; a gentle ramp (15 degrees) leads down to a level landing; the portal is a timbered opening (box-built sets and a lintel) through a dry-stone headwall 1 m thick, the Company's grille at its back with one lamp; the cutting and the adit drain inward: rain on the landing runs under the grille in a stone gutter and down the adit's floor, which falls 0.7 m to the foot of the Portal Drive (+3.40), where it sinks through a grated swallet into the limestone below
gates.why: the mine's east adit, where the levels start; Mill Lane has no natural bank, but its ground rises east, so the adit is reached down its own cutting from the outlaws' trail

zones_convention: Trav_ size is the viewer's [sx, sy, sz] in the node's own frame (src/traverse.ts): sx along the passage or, on a climb, the climbable width along the face; sy up; sz across (a crawl's or sidle's width) or, on a climb, the depth through the face plane. The node stands at `centre` (village frame) turned so that its +X points at `x_axis_deg` in plan; `basis` gives its three axes in the village frame and `gltf` the same node in glTF (Y up). A climb node stands on the face plane with +Z out of the wall towards the walker, so -Z points along `mantle_deg`.
